assessment_history.summary: The PRD for "enrich_context_summaries" is thorough, well-structured, and ready for artifact generation. It clearly articulates the problem, solution, scope boundaries, detailed requirements, tech stack, affected files, design decisions, and dependencies. The intent is unambiguous, goals are implicit but derivable from the requirements and problem statement, non-goals are explicitly defined, and background context is richly provided with concrete data (character counts, session audit IDs, real examples). Minor gaps exist around explicit measurable success criteria and ownership, but these do not block implementation.
gaps: No explicit 'Goals' section with measurable success metrics (e.g., target reduction in shallow summaries, prompt budget savings, or qualitative adoption benchmarks). Goals are implied but not formally stated.
No 'owner' field populated — the PRD has an empty owner, which may create accountability gaps.

No rollout or testing strategy described — e.g., how the enriched summaries will be validated for quality before full adoption, or whether there is a plan to evaluate agent behavior change post-deployment.
The ~500–1000 character guideline for summary length is stated as a soft target with no mechanism to detect or alert on systematic under-compliance by agents.

questions.text: Can you define one or more measurable success criteria for this feature?
questions.context: The PRD lacks a formal Goals section. Measurable outcomes help validate whether the feature achieved its intent — e.g., 'X% reduction in trivial summaries stored', 'average summary length increases to Y characters', or 'coder agents reference [CONTEXT] items Z% more often in session outputs'.
options: Reduction in trivially short summaries (< 100 chars) stored per run
Average enriched summary length reaches 500+ characters within N runs
Qualitative review of next 5 runs shows at least 80% of coder summaries contain non-obvious learnings
No formal metric — quality is assessed by manual audit

questions.text: Who is the owner or DRI (Directly Responsible Individual) for this spec?
questions.context: The 'owner' field is empty. Knowing the owner ensures accountability for implementation decisions and review sign-off.

questions.text: Is there a plan to validate the enriched summaries before full deployment — e.g., a shadow mode, manual review gate, or A/B comparison run?
questions.context: The PRD describes behavior changes to both coder prompt instructions and auto-generated summary filtering. A validation step would reduce the risk of inadvertently dropping useful summaries or producing low-quality enriched ones.
options: Manual audit of enriched summaries from the first run after deployment
Side-by-side comparison run with old and new summary generation logic
No formal validation — trust the design and iterate based on future audits
Automated test coverage of compose_enriched_summary() and generate_archetype_summary() is sufficient
